notes: OpenELIS Global 2 is an open-source laboratory information system. It publishes no machine-readable API spec (no springdoc/springfox in pom.xml, no committed whole-API OpenAPI file), so this document was generated from the vendor's own source of truth: the Spring controller surface of DIGI-UW/OpenELIS-Global-2 at commit e57a5339 (3.2.2.0). Every @RestController and every @Controller method carrying @ResponseBody or returning ResponseEntity was extracted with its HTTP verb, class-level and method-level mapping, @PathVariable/@RequestParam parameters and @RequestBody type — 1048 operations under the webapp's servlet context /api/OpenELIS-Global (servers[0]), which is why coverage is 'full': it is the whole declared REST surface, not a hand-picked slice. Completeness is 'best-effort' because response bodies are only modelled where the vendor type is known: 18 named schemas (the core lab-interop objects plus FHIR Bundle/FhirResource/CapabilityStatement/OperationOutcome); every other operation declares an honest untyped or loosely-typed JSON response naming the Java type it serializes, and 'required' flags on those bodies are not claimed at all. servers[1] is the companion HAPI FHIR R4 store (the external-fhir-api service, org.openelisglobal.fhirstore.uri) that OpenELIS deploys alongside the webapp and that holds the same lab work as FHIR resources: it serves /fhir/** with full CRUD, while the webapp proxies read-only queries of those resources under /rest/fhir/** (FhirQueryRestController). Known gaps: the adaptor's own JSDoc example http.get('referral-reasons') has no matching controller in the vendor source — the real endpoint is GET /rest/displayList/REFERRAL_REASONS — and the spec follows the source, not the JSDoc; deployments running an older release than 3.2.2.0 will expose a subset of these paths; and file-upload endpoints taking @ModelAttribute/MultipartFile are declared as untyped multipart bodies.
